title: Michelin-Starred Indienne Brings India's Fine Dining Revolution to New York's Hudson Yards
excerpt: Chef Sujan Sarkar's acclaimed Chicago restaurant lands in Manhattan with three new concepts, signaling Indian cuisine's ascent in America's fine-dining firmament.
body:
When Chef Sujan Sarkar opens the doors of Indienne New York on May 28, he will not merely be launching another restaurant. He will be making a statement about where Indian cuisine belongs in America's culinary hierarchy — at the very top.

## From Chicago's River North to Hudson Yards

Indienne first arrived in Chicago's River North neighbourhood at the end of 2022. Within a year, it had earned a Michelin star, becoming the first-ever starred Indian restaurant in the Chicago area and one of only four across the United States. Now, the 34-seat tasting-menu destination is expanding to Hudson Yards, taking up residence on the second floor of Henry Hall, a luxury residential tower at 515 West 38th Street.

But Sarkar is not stopping at one concept. Alongside Indienne, he is launching Apas, a craft cocktail bar infused with South Asian botanicals, and Elder, a British-Indian chophouse inspired by his years cooking in London's top kitchens. All three will operate under the Henry Hall roof, with Apas and Elder slated to open later this summer.

## A Homecoming With Edge

For Sarkar, this is a return to the city where his American journey began. In 2017, he opened Baar Baar, a modern Indian gastrobar in the East Village, before expanding to Chicago, Los Angeles, and San Francisco. "I wanted to come back to New York with something new and more progressive," he told DiningOut. "Coming back with Indienne feels like both a homecoming and a new beginning."

The New York menu will offer multi-course tasting experiences in non-vegetarian, pescatarian, vegetarian, and vegan formats — a nod to India's vast dietary diversity and an acknowledgment that modern diners expect flexibility without compromise. Signature dishes like the Oyster Pani Puri and an upscale take on paneer kofta with summer squash hint at Sarkar's approach: classical European technique married to the depth and complexity of Indian spice.

## The Bigger Picture for Desi Diners

For the Indian diaspora in America, Indienne's expansion carries a significance beyond the plate. For decades, Indian restaurants in the US occupied a narrow band — either budget buffets or neighbourhood curry houses. The emergence of Michelin-starred Indian establishments, from Semma in New York to Rania in Washington, D.C., represents a generational shift.

Sarkar is explicit about his ambitions. He wants Indienne to be part of a movement that elevates Indian cuisine globally, not just within the desi community. "I think New Yorkers deserve something a little cutting-edge," he said. For NRIs who have long navigated the gap between the sophistication of Indian food culture and its perception abroad, restaurants like Indienne are a point of pride.

## What's Next

Reservations for Indienne New York are available via SevenRooms, with seatings Tuesday through Saturday starting at 5 p.m. The cocktail bar Apas and the chophouse Elder will follow in the coming months, creating a three-concept destination that could become one of Hudson Yards' most distinctive dining addresses. With only four Michelin-starred Indian restaurants in the country, the stakes — and the expectations — are high.

*Sources: DiningOut, WhatNow NYC, Restaurant Business Online*
author: Diaspora Desk
